transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I, um... I'm just here because... well, they have me helping out with the safety trainings at the plant lately. And... I just keep noticing my hands. When I'm pointing at the diagrams or the equipment, they just look so... wrinkly. And uneven. I can't really stop looking at them. And then... I don't know, there was a photo of me in the company newsletter, and my face just looked crooked. I mentioned it to a few people, but they said they didn't see it. But... it's just bothering me, I guess.
Do you find yourself feeling especially anxious or self-conscious when you're in front of other people, like during these safety trainings?

Well... maybe a little. I mean, I still do my job. It hasn't stopped me from working or doing the trainings. But... I guess I am a bit slower getting ready on those days. Just... trying to fix things, I guess. And I definitely step out of the way if someone brings out a camera now. I don't know, I just... find myself hesitating before going to get-togethers I used to enjoy. It's just easier to stay back sometimes.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in activities you used to enjoy, even outside of the social situations at work?
No... I wouldn't say that. I still do my normal routine at home, and... I still like the things I usually do. It's really just... what I mentioned before.
Do you believe that the wrinkles on your hands or the crookedness of your face are very noticeable to others, even if they don’t mention it?
I... I don't know. I guess I just assume they see it. I mean, they have to, right? But... they don't say anything. So, maybe they don't. I'm not really sure.
Do you feel like others must notice or be repulsed by these things you mentioned, even if they don’t say anything about them?
Repulsed? No... I wouldn't say that. I don't think they're repulsed. I just... I really don't know what they're thinking. Like I said, nobody brings it up, so... I just don't know.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time thinking about these concerns with your appearance, like checking your hands or face repeatedly, trying to hide them, or comparing yourself to others?

I suppose... I do check a bit. If I'm going to a class, or... maybe a workshop at the senior center, I'll go to the bathroom mirror first. Just a few times. I put lotion on my hands... turn my head to see how it looks. Sometimes I'll ask someone I work with if I look okay. It... makes me run a little late sometimes, but I still get there.

Do you worry that the wrinkles on your hands or the way your face looks in photos are signs of something being seriously wrong with your appearance, even if others don’t notice or seem concerned about it?

Seriously wrong? Um... no. I wouldn't say that. 

I don't think it means there's something majorly wrong with me. I just... I just don't like how it looks. That's all. It's just... getting older, I guess. I don't really think of it as a serious sign of anything.
Are your concerns mainly about these specific things — your hands looking wrinkly and your face looking crooked — or do you worry about other parts of your appearance as well?

Um... well, it's mostly those things. I guess it really started bothering me when I had to help out with the safety trainings at work. I'm pointing at things, showing people what to do, and... I just keep looking at my hands. They just look so wrinkly and uneven to me. And then... I saw some photos of me in the company newsletter, and my face just looked crooked. I don't really know why. People tell me they don't see it, but... I don't know. That's mostly what I focus on.
Do you feel a lot of distress or discomfort because of how you perceive your hands or face, like it's really hard to stop thinking about it or it interferes with your day?

Um... I don't know about distress. I still go to work. I still volunteer. It hasn't stopped me from doing any of that. 

I guess... I am a little slower getting ready for the trainings now. And... well, I do try to duck out of photos if I can. Or I might hesitate a bit before going out to social things I used to just go to. But... I still manage.
Are you mainly concerned about how your hands and face look, or do you also feel self-conscious about other aspects of your appearance, like your weight, hair, or other body parts?

Um... no, not really. It's just... what I said before. 

It's just the hands and the face. Ever since I started doing those safety trainings, I just... I can't stop noticing my hands when I'm pointing at the equipment. They just look so wrinkly and uneven to me. And then... the newsletter photos. My face just looks crooked. I don't really worry about my weight or my hair or anything like that. Just... those two things. Even though people say I look fine, it just... it bothers me.

When you're worried about your hands or face during the trainings or events, is your main concern that others will judge or think negatively about you, or is it more about how you see those parts of your body not looking right, even if others don’t seem to notice?

Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't thought about it like that. 

I guess... I just don't like how they look. I don't really know what other people are thinking about me. It just... it doesn't look right to me. That's all.
Do you believe that the way your hands or face look is a big problem that others must notice, even though they don’t seem to mention it or act like it's a concern?

I don't know about a big problem. But... yes, I think they must see it. 

I mean, that's why I'm here, I guess. Ever since I started doing those safety trainings, it's just... all I see. My hands pointing at the machines, they just look so wrinkly. And the skin looks uneven. And then... the photos for the newsletter. My face just looks crooked to me. I know people say they don't see it, but... I don't know how they couldn't. It's just right there.
Do you believe that these things you notice about your hands and face — the wrinkles and the crookedness — are things that others should easily see, even if they tell you they don’t notice them?

I... I don't really know. I'm not sure what other people should be able to see. 

I just... I know what it looks like to me. I can't really speak for them. That's all.

When you're worried about your hands or face during the trainings or events, is your main concern that others will judge or think negatively about you, or is it more about how you personally see those parts of your body not looking right, even if others don’t seem to notice?
I think... you just asked me that. I don't really have a different answer. I just... I don't like how they look to me. I'm not really worried about what other people are thinking, I just... I see it.
Would you say that your main concern is about how your hands and face look to you personally, or is it more about how others might see or judge them?
I... I thought I just answered that. Like I said, it's just how they look to me. I'm not really thinking about other people. I don't really know what else to say about it.
Do you find yourself doing things like checking your hands or face often, applying lotions, or changing your appearance in any way because of these concerns?

I mean... I guess I do check sometimes. Like before a class, or if we have a workshop at the senior center... I might stop by the bathroom mirror a few times. 

I just... I'll put some lotion on my hands. Maybe turn my head a bit to see how my face looks in the light. Sometimes I'll ask one of the other workers if I look okay. It... it makes me run a little late sometimes, but I still get there. I don't think it's a big deal.
Do you feel that the wrinkles on your hands or the crookedness of your face are flaws that make your appearance unacceptable to you, even if others don't seem to notice or react to them?

I... well, yes. That's... that's why I'm here, I guess. Ever since I started helping out with those safety trainings at work, I just... I can't stop staring at my hands when I'm pointing at the manuals. They just look so... wrinkly. And uneven. 

And then... they take pictures for the company newsletter, and I look at my face and it just... it looks crooked to me. I know other people say they don't see it, but... I see it. It just bothers me.
